subject: MSA & Order Form — open-source/model license liability: cap scope and carve-outs
summary: External prospect flagged liability language related to open-source models and third-party licensor pass-throughs. Redwood legal proposed narrowed pass-throughs and carve-outs to preserve damage cap while accommodating customer's reqs. Procurement timeline and SOC2 evidence items discussed.
messages:
From: Sara Keller <sara.keller@acmerobotics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Voss <tom.voss@vendorlegal.io>
Date: 2026-11-13T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Draft MSA + Order Form - Liability questions

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. Legal reviewed the MSA and has two big open items before procurement can sign:

1) The cap on liability in Section 8 — we need clarity whether liabilities flowing from third-party open-source licensors can be passed through so that Acme can seek the same remedies against the underlying licensor.
2) The exclusion for consequential damages — we understand the standard waiver, but our product team is pushing for an explicit carve-out where open-source license obligations (e.g., GPL-style warranty/indemnity triggers) are not treated as "consequential" and therefore recoverable.

I've attached our redline and a short note from procurement on timeline. Can your counsel confirm whether Redwood is willing to accept a limited pass-through for OSS licensor claims or to carve them out of the cap for third-party IP liabilities?

We'd like to get to an answer by end of week to keep the November renewal.

Best,
Sara Keller
Head of Procurement, Acme Robotics
attachment: Acme_Robotics_MSA_redline_v1.docx

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sara Keller <sara.keller@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA + Order Form - Liability questions

Hi Sara — thanks for the redline and the note. Looping in our legal lead (Priyom) and contracts (Rishi) so we can give a consolidated response.

Quick context from product side: Acme will be ingesting several community models and a small number of third-party plugins; their ask is to make claims relating to OSS licensor obligations recoverable (either via pass-through or via carve-out from the aggregate liability cap).

Priyom / Rishi — can you review Acme's proposed language and advise whether Redwood can:
- permit a narrow pass-through to cover third-party OSS licensors' claims tied to licensed models/plugins, limited to direct IP infringement or indemnity obligations (not general indemnities); OR
- alternatively, carve those specific OSS liabilities out of Redwood's liability cap (and retain the overall cap for other contract claims).

I've attached the customer's redline for reference. Sara, we'll circle back with proposed phrasing and any additional info we need.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
attachment: Acme_Robotics_MSA_redline_v1.docx

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Keller <sara.keller@acmerobotics.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T08:37:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Draft MSA + Order Form - Liability questions

Team / Sara — reviewed Acme's redline. High-level thoughts and a suggested approach below. See attached redline_suggestion_oss_clause.docx for inline wording.

1) Narrow pass-through vs carve-out:
- We should avoid open-ended pass-through language (too much exposure). Instead propose a limited pass-through that applies only where (a) the claim is directly caused by a licensed third-party model or plugin distributed by Redwood to Acme; (b) the claim arises from a breach of an express license term or an indemnity obligation by the third-party licensor; and (c) Redwood has no contractual remedy (e.g., licensor insolvent).

Proposed short-form: "Notwithstanding the liability cap, claims arising solely from third-party open-source licensor obligations (limited to direct IP infringement and express indemnities under the applicable license) shall not be subject to the cap, provided Redwood has used commercially reasonable efforts to obtain indemnification from the licensor and notifies Customer promptly upon receipt of such claim."

2) Consequential damages carve-out:
- We can keep the general consequential-damages waiver but carve out direct damages and expressly exclude from the waiver any liabilities that are obligations of a third-party licensor under their license (i.e., those are recoverable). This keeps our upstream exposure contained while addressing Acme's procurement ask.

3) Monetary cap mechanics:
- Keep a single aggregate cap tied to fees (e.g., 12 months of fees) but exclude the limited OSS/licensor liabilities from that aggregation. Also add a per-claim subcap if Acme insists.

4) Operational mitigations:
- Recommend adding contractual obligations for Redwood to (a) maintain a list of included third-party models/plugins and their licenses; (b) provide license metadata and provenance at contract signature; and (c) provide timely remediation or substitution if a covered model is later found to be problematic. These reduce Acme's need for broad pass-through.

5) Evidence / procurement asks:
- Sara asked about SOC 2 and audit artifacts. Rishi / Lauren: please confirm what we can share given hosted/dedicated differences.

Next steps: I propose we send Sara the redline with the language above and a short explanation of why this scoped approach balances commercial risk. If Acme insists on broader pass-through, escalate to commercial leadership for approval of increased cap and insurance layering.

Attachment: redline_suggestion_oss_clause.docx; OSS-license-checklist.xlsx

- Priyom
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Keller <sara.keller@acmerobotics.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Draft MSA + Order Form - Liability questions

+1 to Priyom's suggested approach. A couple of practical edits from contracts:
- Replace "commercially reasonable efforts to obtain indemnification from the licensor" with a clearer "good-faith, documented attempts to obtain indemnity from the licensor within 30 days of notice" to give us an objective trigger.
- Add a requirement that any pass-through claim must be accompanied by (i) the license identifier and copy of the license, (ii) a clear chain of custody showing Redwood distributed the specific model/plugin to Customer, and (iii) proof that Customer complied with any downstream license obligations.

If Acme is okay with the narrow pass-through + the documentation requirement, we can accept the carve-out without increasing the base cap. If they push for no documentation or unconstrained pass-through, we'll need to propose a higher cap (suggest 24 months of fees) and add notice/defense cooperation specifics.

I'll incorporate these edits into Priyom's redline and send back to Sara.

- Rishi
Senior Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
attachment: redline_suggestion_oss_clause.docx

From: Sara Keller <sara.keller@acmerobotics.com>

Subject: RE: Draft MSA + Order Form - Liability questions

Thanks — that helps a lot. The procurement team is comfortable with a narrow, documented pass-through and the 30-day documentation window you suggested, provided we get the license metadata at signing and a living list of included third-party models/plugins.

Two quick items before I run this with execs: (1) can you confirm whether Redwood can produce SOC 2 Type II evidence for hosted versus dedicated deployments (we're in hosted today but may move to dedicated in six months); (2) can you confirm there will be a clause that Redwood will attempt remediation/substitution for a covered model if a problematic license event occurs (per Priyom's suggestion)?

If you can confirm those two points in writing today, procurement will clear to move to final signatures next week.

Appreciate the quick turn.

Sara
Head of Procurement, Acme Robotics
